No family in PA-1—or anywhere in America—should have to fear the water coming out of their tap.

PFAS “forever chemicals” have seeped into our community’s water—endangering health and sticking families with costs they should never bear.

As Co-Founder and Co-Chair of the bipartisan PFAS Task Force, I have been working with community members and local organizations to deliver millions for cleanup, press the Pentagon to accelerate remediation, and introduce bipartisan legislation to give the EPA’s first-ever PFAS drinking water standards the force of law.

Today, I’ve introduced the PURE Water Act—a bipartisan bill that funds municipal water treatment upgrades to remove PFAS at the source, protect families, restore trust, and ensure polluters—not taxpayers—pay.

Safe water is non-negotiable. From Bucks County to communities nationwide, I’ll keep fighting until clean water is guaranteed for all.

🔗Read more: https://t.co/eJtljuEth9

ICYMI: PFAS “forever chemicals” remain one of the most urgent public health challenges facing our nation.

These contaminants have infiltrated drinking water systems—including here in PA-1—causing serious health risks and forcing municipalities to shoulder costs they did not create.

As Co-Founder and Co-Chair of the bipartisan PFAS Task Force, I’ve advanced policies to:

✅ Secure federal cleanup funding for local communities
✅ Press the Pentagon to accelerate remediation at defense sites
✅ Introduce bipartisan legislation codifying EPA’s first-ever PFAS drinking water standards

Now, I’ve introduced the PURE Water Act—a bipartisan, targeted solution that invests in municipal water treatment upgrades to remove PFAS at the source, strengthen public health protections, and hold polluters—not taxpayers—financially responsible.

🔗 Read More: https://t.co/QX1WwNp1cG

Joe Fiandra wore our nation’s uniform with honor, fought amyloidosis with courage, and faced barriers in our health care system that no family should ever endure.

When I sat down with his wife Helen and the Fiandra family in Warrington, they asked me to ensure no other family had to fight that fight.

That’s why I introduced the Joe Fiandra Access to Home Infusion Act of 2025—bipartisan legislation to expand Medicare so seniors can receive life-saving infusion drugs and equipment at home—surrounded by loved ones, with dignity and compassion.

This closes a critical gap created under the 21st Century Cures Act, and will  make sure families get the care they deserve.

Proud to lead this effort with @DrNealDunnFL2 and @RepDarrenSoto alongside the Fiandra family and entire amyloidosis community.

🔗 Read more: https://t.co/E6NZI5q9yH

Tony Montalto and Tom Hoyer turned unimaginable loss into a national movement. As founders of @StandWParkland, they’ve become the leading voices for safer schools and stronger mental health supports across America.

I’m proud to stand with my friends as we continue our partnership to turn tragedy into action and protect every child, educator, and family. Together we’re advancing a comprehensive approach; from modernizing school security to ensuring every student has access to a mental health professional who can recognize and prevent a crisis before it happens.

As Co-Chair of the Bipartisan Mental Health and Substance Use Disorder Task Force, I’ve made this a top priority. My Mental Health in Schools Excellence Program Act tackles this crisis by:

✅ Expanding school-based mental health services
✅ Creating a tuition-matching program to train more psychologists, counselors, and social workers
✅ Prioritizing high-need schools and underserved students
✅ Addressing the fact that nearly 38% of students lack sufficient access to mental health professionals

We’re also working to champion the Measure for Safer School Districts Act to deliver 21st-century security and emergency response to every school, and the EAGLES Act to expand the Secret Service’s threat assessment network, giving schools the tools to stop violence before it starts.

Thank you to these two remarkable men for the their longtime partnership and friendship. We will continue working to build a future where every student can learn without fear and every parent can send their child to school with peace of mind.

Health care reform starts with advocates like our own Maygan Best of New Hope, who turn personal battles into public action.

Today, I joined Maygan and the @CrohnsColitisFn to focus on real, actionable solutions. We discussed the Safe Step Act, which I co-sponsor, to end dangerous step therapy delays and ensure patients receive the treatments their doctors prescribe, not what insurance companies dictate, and the protecting research funding, because life-changing treatments and cures can only happen when science is supported, not sidelined.

This is how change happens: patients leading, communities rallying, and lawmakers listening. I’ll look forward to working alongside Maygan, the CCF Foundation, and families across PA-1 to ensure no one’s care is delayed, denied, or out of reach.

Medical research drives innovation, strengthens our economy, and saves lives.

This week, I met with Yardley’s own Lara Flynn and national leaders from the @RallyForNIH to chart a path forward. Together, we emphasized the urgent need for robust, sustained NIH funding in the FY26 budget, and the bipartisan responsibility to complete appropriations on time to avoid costly delays that stall breakthroughs, slow clinical trials, and put patient care at risk.

Medical research is one of the smartest, highest-impact investments we can make. I remain committed to working alongside advocates, scientists, and families across PA-1 to protect progress, prevent disruption, and ensure America leads the world in discovery and cures.

I’ve met with families and advocates from across our district who are living with migraine and other headache disorders. They’ve shared how these conditions disrupt their lives and how invisible they can feel in our health care system. 

With more than 40 million Americans affected—the leading cause of disability worldwide and the top cause of disability for U.S. women under 50–it’s clear we need a national response shaped by patients, providers, and advocates.

Together, @RepLoriTrahan and I have introduced the first-ever federal initiative built from those conversations to deliver real change.

Our bipartisan bill:

✅ Creates the National Headache Disorders Initiative within HHS to coordinate care and research across federal agencies
✅ Builds the workforce and expands access to diagnosis and treatment, especially in underserved areas
✅ Improves data and drives public education to reduce stigma and guide smarter policy
✅ Establishes a new Advisory Council of agency leaders, patient advocates, providers, and researchers to keep the community’s voice at the center of national policy

This bipartisan bill will turns decades of neglect into a coordinated federal plan to improve care and drive solutions nationwide. 

🔗 Read More Here: https://t.co/NMBtIKTVMl

Strong community mental health care starts with trusted leaders, and Jon Rubin is one of the best.
 
This morning, I met with Jon, CEO of Penndel Mental Health Center, a vital partner and non-profit mental health center that has served our community for over 50 years. Beyond treatment, PHMC provides comprehensive mental and behavioral health care and critical advocacy for individuals and families struggling with mental illness, intellectual disabilities, substance use, and co-occurring disorders.
 
As Co-Chair of the Bipartisan Mental Health and Substance Use Disorder Task Force, Jon and I have worked together over the years in our shared mission, and his local insight has directly informed the national policies I champion. From protecting funding, expanding access, and ensuring that care is not delayed or denied, I am grateful for his partnership and look forward to continuing our work together to ensure every individual and family in our community has the support, resources, and care they need.

Today, I visited two of our region’s most vital pediatric institutions, Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia and St. Christopher’s Hospital for Children, for a critical conversation on the future of children’s health care and the mounting challenges facing pediatric hospitals nationwide.

For decades, @ChildrensPhila and St. Chris have delivered world-class, compassionate care to hundreds of thousands of children and families in our community and across the Commonwealth, regardless of background, income, or diagnosis. From breakthroughs in rare disease treatment to everyday care that keeps kids healthy, their work doesn’t just heal—it saves lives. 

Yet the critical care they provide is increasingly under strain. The widening gap between rising costs and Medicaid shortfalls is pushing even our strongest safety-net hospitals to a breaking point.

I’ve always fought to protect and strengthen Medicaid and CHIP, and I’ll continue working closely with the exceptional leadership teams at CHOP and St. Chris to ensure they have the resources, support, and long-term stability they need. That includes championing the Accelerating Kids’ Access to Care Act of 2025, which I am proud to co-sponsor, advancing a special Medicaid designation for children’s hospitals, and securing greater NIH investment in pediatric research. Our children’s health is non-negotiable, and I’ll keep working to ensure these institutions can continue their lifesaving mission without compromise. @hospitals4kids

Great meeting today with the @NationalCouncil for Mental Wellbeing (NCMW) and our own Katy Morton of Hatfield to discuss challenges facing our behavioral health providers across our country. 

We focused on strengthening the foundation of our behavioral health system—stabilizing funding, improving recruitment and retention, and ensuring providers have the support they need to deliver quality care. As Co-Chair of the Bipartisan Mental Health and Substance Use Disorder Task Force, I have been working to translate these priorities into policies that expand access, strengthen the workforce, and ensure communities can rely on consistent, compassionate care.

I’m grateful to NCMW and Katy for their partnership in this shared mission. Supporting those on the frontlines of care will remain one of my highest priorities because when we strengthen our mental health workforce, we strengthen the foundation of every community.

The mental health crisis isn’t somewhere else—it’s here in our schools, neighborhoods, and homes. And too often, the hardest part isn’t asking for help. It’s finding it.

As Co-Chair of the Bipartisan Mental Health and Substance Use Disorder Task Force, I’ve made it a priority to make care accessible and immediate. From securing funding for the Bright Path Center in Doylestown, Pennsylvania’s first crisis stabilization center, to advancing bipartisan legislation like the Expanding Access to Mental Health in Schools Act, the Mental Health in Schools Excellence Program Act, and the Barriers to Suicide Act, I’m working to build a system that reaches people early and prevents crisis.

Today, on World Mental Health Day, may we use this moment to come together—not just in recognition, but in shared commitment to act with compassion and urgency.

America’s mental health and substance use crisis demands action—not retreat.

The reported reduction-in-force at the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) is unacceptable and dangerous. As soon as reports surfaced, I reached out to our partners on the frontlines to coordinate our response and ensure their voices are heard at the federal level. SAMHSA is a cornerstone of our national behavioral health response — driving prevention, treatment, crisis services, and the data that guides smart policy. Undermining it means weakening the very network that connects people to care when they need it most.

I’m pressing for answers and accountability, and pushing for a clear plan to protect these critical services. As Co-Chair of the Bipartisan Mental Health and Substance Use Disorder Task Force, I intend to use every tool at my disposal to ensure SAMHSA can do what it was built to do: save lives and support our communities.

I joined @johnrobertsFox on @AmericaRpts to talk through the bipartisan Senate agreement, the roadmap ahead in working together to drive down health care costs, and why we must always reject government shutdowns as a negotiating tactic.

They don’t shape policy. They inflict harm on the very people we are sworn to serve.

Let’s end this. Reopen the government. And stay focused on delivering for the American people —not using them as leverage.

Watch below ⬇️:

Freedom endures because of remarkable men and women like these.

Today, at The Manor at Yorktown in Jamison, and at the Pine Run Health Center in Doylestown, we had the privilege of honoring 28 veterans who defended our great nation with courage, bravery, unwavering commitment—some of the finest Americans in not only our PA-1 community, but our entire country. 

They served to defend freedom. They stood watch so others could live in peace. And even now, continue to remind us what it means to live a life of purpose, grounded in service to something greater than ourselves.

We owe them more than thanks.

We owe them humble honor—in how we live, how we serve, and how we stand united as a community and as a country. 🇺🇸

Modernizing care coordination for Medicare patients has been one of my top health care priorities—and yesterday’s Ways & Means Health Subcommittee hearing underscored exactly why this work must continue.

Chronic disease now defines the Medicare population. Yet instead of coordinated care, seniors are facing:

✔️50% more specialist visits than two years ago
✔️ Thousands in preventable costs per patient
✔️ Physicians stretched too thin to focus on quality care

I focused my questioning to Dr. Michael Hoben and Dr. Ashish Parikh on two reforms I’ve been driving:

1️⃣ Making telehealth a permanent pillar of chronic care
2️⃣ Modernizing Medicare’s physician payment system

Their message was clear:

✔ Telehealth is a core tool for stabilizing chronic disease, avoiding emergencies, and lowering costs
✔ Value-based models measurably improve outcomes—from higher screening rates to fewer hospitalizations—while saving Medicare money

When telehealth payments briefly lapsed during the shutdown, we saw how quickly access can be disrupted. Permanent telehealth reliability and a modern payment system must remain central to this work, and I will continue driving it forward.

From the outset, I committed to delivering a bipartisan solution to prevent end-of-year ACA premium spikes—and today, alongside a bipartisan group of lawmakers, we are doing exactly that.

Our Bipartisan Health Insurance Affordability Act keeps ACA premium tax credits in place so families aren’t blindsided by sudden, unaffordable increases in the coverage they rely on. It’s a practical, people-first fix that prevents an immediate crisis and protects families now while preserving the space to keep working toward a stronger, smarter, more affordable healthcare system.

Responsible governance means securing 80 percent of what families need today rather than risking 100 percent of nothing tomorrow. We built this the right way, with input from across the aisle and across chambers, with the clearest pathway to the President’s desk. We’re ready to get this done, and we call on our colleagues to step up, join us, and put American families—not political messaging—first.

🔗 Read More: https://t.co/pfTz7QG4UH

This morning, I joined CNBC’s Squawk Box with my fellow @ProbSolvCaucus Co-Chair @RepTomSuozzi to discuss my Bipartisan Health Insurance Affordability Act. Yesterday, we filed a discharge petition to ensure the House has both the opportunity and the obligation to vote. Every member must decide whom they serve: the people, or the politics.

Our bill delivers:

✔️ A 2-year extension of ACA premium tax credits preventing a major premium spike and providing the runway to improve our healthcare system for the long term. 
✔️ Targeted relief for working families by restoring income limits. Unlike current law, subsidies will no longer flow to high earners.
✔️ Real PBM reform to bring accountability to the intermediaries inflating prescription drug prices.
✔️ Modernized HSAs that put individuals back in control:
— Unlike current law, HSA dollars can be used to pay premiums.
— Unlike current law, unused HSA funds roll over every year.

For months, I’ve worked with Republicans and Democrats in both chambers, with input from the Administration, to build a two-party, responsible, realistic solution that can actually pass—not a messaging bill.

This is the moment for Congress to choose whether it will protect working families or permit a crisis we can stop.
I’m firmly on the side of the American people, and I urge my colleagues to join us.

Yesterday, U.S. service members were attacked in Syria, killing three Americans. Having served in the region as a counter-terrorism agent and now on the House Intelligence Committee, I joined Jon Scott to discuss our response, as well as my Bipartisan Health Insurance Affordability Act, and our efforts to deliver targeted relief to middle- and low-income families.

🔗 Watch our full conversation here: https://t.co/XIJZrCHy8l

Joe Fiandra wore our nation’s uniform with honor. He fought amyloidosis with courage. And when his family needed care the most, they were met with barriers in our health care system that never should have existed.

When I sat down with Joe’s wife, Helen, and the Fiandra family in Warrington, they asked me for one thing: make sure no other family ever has to fight that same fight.

That conversation became the Joe Fiandra Access to Home Infusion Act of 2025.

This bipartisan legislation expands Medicare so seniors can receive life-saving infusion drugs and equipment at home, surrounded by loved ones, with dignity, comfort, and compassion. It closes a critical gap created under the 21st Century Cures Act and corrects a system that made care harder when it should have made it easier.

Last week, the @WaysandMeansGOP passed my bill, bringing us one step closer to delivering the care families deserve. 

I am grateful for the support of @RepJasonSmith and my colleagues, and proud to stand with the Fiandra family—let’s finish the job.

This morning, I joined @ShannonBream on @FoxNewsSunday, along with my friend and fellow @ProbSolveCaucus Co-Chair @RepTomSuozzi, to discuss the ongoing ACA and broader health care negotiations.

For months, we did the work—across the aisle, in both chambers, and closely aligned with the White House framework—to build a responsible two-party solution: a targeted two-year extension with income caps, focused relief for working families, modernized HSAs, and real guardrails against fraud.

That plan deserved a vote. Leadership didn’t allow one.

So we made the only call left on the table: move a vehicle to the Senate. Not as the final word—but as a bridge. A way to keep negotiations alive and give the Senate the opportunity to advance a solution that mirrors the original bipartisan agreement we already forged.

These are families we know. Neighbors we serve. And allowing a preventable affordability crisis was, and will never be, an acceptable option.

🔗 Watch here: https://t.co/tOeSM0Exza
